revised_comments: Burkina Faso does not operate a national digital address register, but a municipal addressing programme (adressage urbain), financed by the European Union and implemented with the Association des Municipalités du Burkina Faso, has digitised street and building numbering in parts of Ouagadougou and in Bobo-Dioulasso since 2021. As of April 2025 the scheme had digitised three of Ouagadougou's twelve arrondissements (around 16,300 streets and 93,000 numbered doors), with a further two arrondissements under way; it has not been extended nationwide or to other secondary towns.

revised_comments: Business creation in Burkina Faso is processed through the Centres de Formalités des Entreprises (CEFORE), a one-stop shop where a business simultaneously obtains its commercial register number (RCCM) and its Unique Financial Identifier (IFU) for tax purposes. revised_comments: Formal tax registration of businesses in Burkina Faso remains low relative to the total business population. The national statistics institute's seventh industrial and commercial census (RIC VII, 2016) found registration rates of 13.3% for the commercial register (RCCM), 12.3% for the Unique Financial Identifier (IFU), and 9.9% for social security registration, against a total of 99,261 enumerated businesses, of which only 9.1% met the full definition of formality. The 2026 General Business Census similarly found that 96.5% of the 389,172 economic units identified nationally operate informally. On this basis, digital tax registration covers well under 20% of all businesses operating in the country.
